title: streamline-artifact-traceability-release-metadata-generator
author: Asha Kapoor
description: Context: Private deployments require unambiguous artifact traceability across air-gapped and VPC installs. Current private-installer release objects contain multiple ad-hoc provenance links (SBOM, cosine signatures, bucket paths) that are hard to reconcile during upgrades and complicate automated rollback decisions. This PR introduces a release-metadata-generator service and a deterministic stamp that consolidates build provenance, signing metadata, and environment-specific deployment hints into a single release-metadata.json artifact for every private-installer CI build. Motivation: 1) Enable deterministic upgrade planning (compute a deterministic delta between released bundles). 2) Make rollback decisions machine-readable (contain fallback candidates, gating windows, KMS key IDs). 3) Reduce manual forensics after failed upgrades by surfacing canonical provenance at release time. What this PR does: - Add a release-metadata-generator binary invoked by the CI pipeline that:   * collects SBOM pointers, cosign/TUF attestations, and builder provenance (git ref, build image digest)   * computes a content-addressable stamp for the release bundle using SHA256 over a canonical manifest ordering   * emits release-metadata.json and an index.yaml entry that includes a canonical provenance URL and verifier hints - Injects release-metadata.json into the Helm chart packaging step and the terraform artifact index so private installer upgrades and the on-prem operator can reconcile artifacts atomically - Adds a lightweight validator (release-metadata-verify) used by preflight to verify signatures, KMS key IDs, and deterministic stamp before a staged upgrade - Updates the release CI to upload the release-metadata.json to the artifact registry and attach provenance links to the release Git tag Checklist: - [x] release-metadata-generator binary + unit tests - [x] CI integration (new job: publish-release-metadata) - [x] Helm chart packaging change to include metadata - [x] Terraform module index entry updated - [x] preflight verification hook - [x] docs: README for release metadata and verification usage Compatibility & security notes: - The stamp algorithm is versioned (v1) and documented in docs/release-metadata/README.md so future stamp formats can be introduced without breaking older installers. - Key IDs are recorded but no private keys or secrets are embedded in metadata. KMS/HSM key references are echoed as identifiers only. - Default CI behaviour is opt-in until the next scheduled release window to allow a canary rollout on a small set of clusters Migration plan: - New CI jobs will produce release-metadata.json alongside existing artifacts. - Private installer versions prior to the metadata-aware operator will ignore the extra file. - When the operator (v1.42) is rolled out, it will prefer releases with release-metadata.json for deterministic upgrades. Related: SUP-3142 (customer rollback debug), ENG-4291 (upgrade planner), SEC-92 (provenance policy).

review_comments: Liam: Asked to make the stamp algorithm stable across available go versions; suggested using a stable JSON canonicalizer and adding explicit field ordering. Marisol: Flagged a potential race when multiple artifact uploaders tag the same release; requested idempotent upload semantics and a retry backoff. Evan: Asked for more unit tests around invalid or missing KMS key IDs; requested clearer error messages from release-metadata-verify. Author replies: implemented canonical JSON ordering, added a mutex to the upload step in CI, added 4 more unit tests and clearer errors. Final approval from Liam and Marisol after CI green.
ci_checks: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration-tests: pass (helm package + terraform index), lint: pass, security-scan: pass; one flaky e2e failed on first run (timeout) and was rerun and passed
release_notes: Introduces release-metadata.json (v1) for private-installer releases. Adds CI job publish-release-metadata and preflight verification. Improves artifact traceability for deterministic upgrades and rollbacks. No behavioral changes for existing installers until operator v1.42 is deployed.
notes_for_oncall: If a rollout shows mismatched stamps in preflight, check artifacts in the registry for missing release-metadata.json and confirm the CI publish-release-metadata job completed for the release tag. Use release-metadata-verify locally to validate stamp and KMS references.
